title: Design System: Amazon Price Tracker & Refund Assistant

headline.purpose: The page title. At 800px and below it is 1.5rem. There is no larger display role.

title.purpose: Section headings at 1.05rem. The shipped heading resolves user-agent bold to the bundled 600. The rail wordmark sets 600 explicitly at 0.98rem.

body.purpose: Interface sentences. The reading measure is 68ch. Margin notes wrap at 36ch.

label.purpose: Column headers in moss. Narrow stacked rows reprint the column name at 0.75rem. Form labels are 0.92rem moss.

meta.purpose: The secondary line under a product, a figure, or a list row. Captions are 0.9rem in the same moss.

figure.purpose: Paid, latest, difference, and estimate amounts in Barlow Condensed 600 with tabular numerals.

stamp.purpose: The uppercase word inside the claim stamp, Barlow Condensed 700 at body size.

motion.name: ink
motion.purpose: A stamp checked less than eight seconds ago fades in from opacity 0.15 and rises 3px. Removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Burgundy ticket-corner button for Check prices, Save settings, and Delete local purchase data.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Ink-stroked button for storing or removing a key, and for loading or removing sample orders.

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Slip field with a moss stroke, shared by text inputs and selects.

narrative.overview:
The window is a local ledger printed on shirt-tissue paper. Burgundy stays on the rail and on the stamp, so the table can be read before the ticket-counter color registers. Barlow carries the sentences. Barlow Condensed carries the money and the stamp.

Density is a claim ticket. Each section opens with a heading and one measured sentence, then a hairline table or a hairline list. On the dashboard, paid, latest, and difference share one row. A right-hand margin holds the guarantee, the last synchronization, and Check prices. Totals stay in that sentence. The page has no hero metric cards, and it does not dress itself as Amazon.

The signature is the claim stamp on each difference. The border is dashed when the price has not been checked, solid when it has, and double when the drop meets the savings threshold. A stamp whose check is less than eight seconds old inks in. That motion is removed when the reader prefers reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Burgundy rail on a tissue ground, with slip reserved for the table sheet and the fields
Barlow for interface text; Barlow Condensed for figures, the stamp, the rail's second line, and code
State is the stamp's line: dashed, solid, or double
The table owns the page; totals are one sentence
Flat sheets: 1px hairlines, no shadows, 2px corners on controls

rules.name: The Rail and Stamp Rule
rules.body: Burgundy is the rail, the primary button, the caret, the selection, and the stamp. It does not fill the page, and there is no second accent.

rules.name: The Tissue and Slip Rule
rules.body: Shirt tissue is the only page ground. Claim slip is the sheet under a table and the fill inside a field.

rules.name: The Condensed Money Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed is for figures, the stamp, the rail's second line, and code. Sentences stay in Barlow.

rules.name: The Sentence Totals Rule
rules.body: A page total is one sentence under the heading. It is not a display numeral and not a row of metric cards.

rules.name: The Ledger Owns the Page Rule
rules.body: The table is the body of the dashboard. The margin is for the guarantee, the last synchronization, and Check prices, and under 800px that margin stacks beneath the table.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces do not cast shadows. A hover changes a fill or a label color. It does not raise the control.

rules.name: The Stamp Line Rule
rules.body: State is the stamp's line. Dashed means not checked. Solid means checked. Double means the drop meets the savings threshold. The word (Not checked, Other offer, Lower, Higher, Unchanged) can change without a new color or a fill.

rules.name: The Ticket Corner Rule
rules.body: Controls and rail links use the 2px ticket corner. The stamp is the only pill.

dos: Do keep burgundy on the rail, the primary button, the caret, the selection, and the stamp.
Do print the page on shirt tissue, and put tables and fields on claim slip.
Do set sentences in Barlow, and set figures in Barlow Condensed 600 with tabular numerals.
Do load Barlow 400 and 600 and Barlow Condensed 600 and 700 from the bundled `@fontsource` files.
Do show each difference as a claim stamp: dashed, solid, or double at 4px.
Do keep a page total in one sentence under the heading, with paid, latest, and difference in one row.
Do separate rows with a 1px tissue hairline and leave the sheet flat.
Do use a 2px ledger-ink focus ring, offset 2px, and switch that ring to slip text on the rail.
Do stack the lower work band at 1100px, and stack the sheet, the table, and the rail at 800px.
Do drop the stamp's ink animation when the reader prefers reduced motion.
donts: Don't add a hero row of metric cards, or a display-size total.
Don't dress the interface as Amazon. No marketplace orange, smile, or store chrome.
Don't use a box-shadow, and don't lift a button, row, or rail on hover.
Don't fill the stamp, or recolor it, to show state. The line form is the state.
Don't request a Barlow weight that is not bundled. Synthesis is off, and Condensed 700 belongs to the stamp.
Don't load the faces from a Google Fonts stylesheet.
